chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from some of his companions, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' becomes menstruating before she performs Tawaf al-Ifadah (the circumambulation for release from Ihram), and her purity occurs on the night of Arafah.' He said: 'If she knows that she will become pure, perform Tawaf al-Ifadah with the House, be released from her Ihram, and join the people, then let her do so.'

key_terms.تَطُوفَ بِالْبَيْتِ: She performs circumambulation of the Kaaba (Tawaf al-Ifadah)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعَةً: A state of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Ihram for Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman in Hajj al-Tamattu' who menstruates before her final Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a woman in Hajj al-Tamattu' who menstruates before Tawaf al-Ifadah, emphasizing that she must wait for purity if she anticipates being able to complete the Tawaf and join the pilgrims in time. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of facilitating religious duties by allowing flexibility in timing when the obstacle (menstruation) is temporary and resolvable before the final rites conclude. The ruling underscores the importance of Tawaf al-Ifadah as the definitive act of exiting Ihram, distinguishing it from earlier circumambulations.
